title: Calibrate the rubric, not just the model
description: Synthetic 120-case slices show exact panel-match, disagreement, abstention, severe-miss, and order-flip counts. The panel is reference evidence, not ground truth.

rubrics.label: Vague 1-5 score
rubrics.detail: Uses labels such as poor, good, and excellent without observable boundaries.
rubrics.decisionRule: Force one score for every case.

rubrics.label: Behavior-anchored labels
rubrics.detail: Names required evidence, disqualifying defects, and examples near each boundary.
rubrics.decisionRule: Choose pass, hold, or fail from observable criteria.

rubrics.label: Anchored plus abstention
rubrics.detail: Uses the same boundaries but routes ambiguous or unsupported cases to review.
rubrics.decisionRule: Choose pass, hold, fail, or needs review.

slices.label: Customer support
slices.detail: Policy-grounded answers with moderate consequence and clear required actions.

slices.label: Medical guidance
slices.detail: High-consequence answers where missing evidence and unsafe certainty must escalate.

slices.label: Multilingual policy
slices.detail: Non-English answers with region-specific terminology and uneven judge familiarity.
